pages.text: A dungeon is a complex $(l)dug under the ground$(): only its entrance shows on the surface, and $(l)ruins, remains and signs$() around it give it away. Go down to the $(l)rotunda$(): three $(item)Rune Locks$() guard the way to the boss.$(br2)Explore the $(l)three wings$(), in any order. Each one ends with a chamber held by a $(l)Rune Warden$(), where a chest holds a $(item)Rune Key$(). Use each key on a lock.
pages.title: Donjons

pages.text: When the three locks shine, the $(item)Guardian Seals$() on the stairs dissolve and the way down to the $(l)arena$() opens. The boss is too strong to be dug around: near it, $(l)Mining Fatigue$() stops your pickaxe.$(br2)The $(l)vault$() behind the arena, in unbreakable $(item)Warded Masonry$(), only opens when the boss dies. Plans and rooms change from one dungeon to the next.

Every boss attack is $(l)announced$(): a circle filling up on the ground (leave it before it is full), a ring running along the floor (jump over it), a marked line (step aside), a sweeping beam ($(l)hide behind a pillar$()).$(br2)At each phase the boss stops, invulnerable, then releases a wave: take a step back. The more players, the more health it has.
pages.title: Combats

pages.text: Unbreakable. The seals on the stairs dissolve when the three Rune Locks shine; those of the vault when the boss dies. Bosses never leave their arena: if you flee, they go back and slowly heal.
